subject: Micro-unit metering + long-history amortization — alignment request
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Micro-unit metering + long-history amortization — alignment request

Hi Lydia,

Thanks again for the product demo earlier this week. Before we finalize the pilot SOW, your billing team and ours asked me to clarify how a few metering rules work for the workload you described — specifically around small/partial calls and long-context amortization. I pulled a short usage sample from your team (attached) and sketched two questions so we can sign off quickly: 

1) Micro-unit rounding: your app makes many very short calls (search/fetch + single-turn summarize). Do you expect these to be billed as full quantum units or aggregated? Our standard quantum today is 64 token units but we can make concessions for high-frequency microcalls.

2) Long-history amortization: you’ve got a 60k-character history stored per user, but only a small prefix is sent per call. Would you prefer that we amortize a pinned context window (keeps a warm KV cache) or that each call separately pays for the prefix recompute?

Quick ask: can your team confirm the average tokens per call and the % of calls that include a >2k token prefix? That’ll let us propose a concrete rounding/playbook for the pilot.

Attachments: acme_usage_sample.csv (2MB)

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acmeretail.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Billing <billing@acmeretail.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Micro-unit metering + long-history amortization — alignment request

Avery,

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers from our side after running the sample through our analytics team: 

- Avg tokens per call (payload + model prompt) = ~42 tokens.
- ~72% of calls are single-turn microcalls under 80 tokens.
- ~15% of calls reference a >2k token prefix (these are typically agent sessions where we pull a long thread).

From a commercial point of view, our finance team is worried about the per-call quantum given the high volume of microcalls. Two things we’d like to explore: 

1) A micro-unit aggregation where calls under 80 tokens get aggregated into 10-second buckets and billed as a single 64-token unit (instead of rounding each call up).
2) For long-history cases, amortize a pinned 4096-token warm cache per active user for a reduced incremental charge (instead of billing the full prefix every call).

Can you confirm whether these two levers are feasible for a 3-month pilot? If so, we’ll route an expedited approval to procurement.

Cheers,
Lydia Chen
Head of ML Integrations, Acme Retail
lydia.chen@acmeretail.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acmeretail.com>, Acme Billing <billing@acmeretail.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 10:25:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Micro-unit metering + long-history amortization — alignment request

On Sat, Nov 15, 2025 at 11:03 AM Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acmeretail.com> wrote:
> From a commercial point of view, our finance team is worried about the per-call quantum given the high volume of microcalls.

Hi all — looping in finance to propose a concrete pilot structure. Summary of our recommended approach (keeps implementation light, measurable):

- Microcall aggregation: implement 15-second aggregation windows for calls < 80 tokens. Aggregated window billed at the standard 64-token quantum. This reduces invoice noise and aligns with how we batch on the runtime.
- Warm-cache amortization: we can expose a "pinned-cache" SKU billed per active user at 4096 tokens equivalent per day. For the pilot, we’ll bill pinned-cache at 25% of the normal per-token rate (reflects cache efficiency).
- Minimums & rounding: apply a monthly microcall floor equal to 10M microcall-equivalent tokens (to prevent anomalous very-low-usage subsidization). If usage exceeds floor, normal per-token billing applies with aggregation/ amortization credits applied.

Pilot commercial terms (3 months):
- 10% pilot discount on base token rate (hosted API).
- Aggregation and pinned-cache rules above enabled for the pilot only.
- Data retention & audit logs: standard 90-day logs included.

Please review; if Lydia and Acme sign off we’ll ship a short amendment and a sample invoice run for month 1.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Pricing & Contracts, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_metering_playbook_v1.pdf (PRD + sample invoice simulations)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acmeretail.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Acme Billing <billing@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 15:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Micro-unit metering + long-history amortization — alignment request

Thanks Ben — and Lydia, very helpful numbers.

Lydia: Acme confirms we can start the pilot with the proposed levers. Two small asks from procurement before we finalize: 
- Can we cap the pinned-cache daily billable users to the number of DAUs reported in the attached CSV for month 1 (to avoid surprise scale charges)?
- For microcall aggregation, can you accept a 30-second window instead of 15s? Their client-side burst pattern will sometimes have 20s gaps and a 15s window might split those.

Ben: if those two tweaks are acceptable, please prepare the amendment and a month-1 sample invoice. We’ll aim to sign by end of week.

On Mon, Nov 17, 2025 at 10:25 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Pilot commercial terms (3 months):
> - 10% pilot discount on base token rate.
> - Aggregation and pinned-cache rules above enabled for the pilot only.
